steps.title: Heat-set inserts
steps.text: Soldering iron with an insert tip, about 220 C for PLA and about 280 C for the PPA-CF puck. Press every M3 x 4 x 5 insert square into its 4.0 mm hole until flush: deck (24), motor plate (2 for the leg bridge, 2 for the can stay, 3 for the gear hood), puck adapter (8 in the rear lip, 2 on the front face for cad-drum's SW_INDEX block), bay (corner bosses, standoffs, clamp posts, perfboard bosses). Let each cool before the next one nearby.
steps.label: deck 100
warnings: frame_cheek_r, frame_motor_adapter rest only on parts placed later (by 'Can stay', 'Gear guards', 'Main shaft: index contact', 'Motor leg' and 1 more)
steps.heading: Step 1 (deck 100): Heat-set inserts

steps.title: Fit the remaining frame parts
steps.text: Parts without an explicit assembly step: frame_perfboard.
steps.heading: Step 2: Fit the remaining frame parts

steps.title: Drill the rover
steps.text: Lay the deck on the rover top plate where it will live (launch direction forward). Mark through the 45 perimeter holes with a 3 mm drill or a scriber (or tape down the 1:1 PDF template from cad/parts/_frame_tests/drill_template.py), take the deck off, drill 3.4 mm. Deburr.
steps.label: deck 101
steps.heading: Step 3 (deck 101): Drill the rover

steps.title: Deck on the rover
steps.text: Slide the tiles together on the dovetails (from above). M3 x 25 SHCS down through every perimeter hole, washer and nyloc under the rover plate. Snug, not crushed. Do this before the other subsystems put their feet down: some rover bolts sit under their feet.
steps.label: deck 102
steps.heading: Step 4 (deck 102): Deck on the rover

steps.title: Motor plate
steps.text: Hold the motor plate upright (front face, the side without the bridge, towards +y) with its bridge against the top of the leg. 2 x M3 x 12 along y through the leg's long counterbores into the bridge inserts.
steps.label: motor 110
steps.heading: Step 5 (motor 110): Motor plate

steps.title: Wiper motor on the puck (bench)
steps.text: Battery unplugged. Put the M6 bolts through the puck slots from the front (heads sit in the slot counterbores), into the motor bosses (threaded bosses, or a nut behind each boss ear). Slide the motor so its shaft is centred in the bore (a 10 mm drill shank in the coupler bore helps), then tighten.
steps.label: motor 111
steps.heading: Step 6 (motor 111): Wiper motor on the puck (bench)

steps.title: Puck into the plate
steps.text: Feed the puck into the plate window from behind (the motor side) until its lip sits on the plate's rear face. From the front, M3 x 12 through the plate into the lip inserts (8 of the 8 rim holes have both plate and lip; use those).
steps.label: motor 112
steps.heading: Step 7 (motor 112): Puck into the plate

steps.title: Motor leg
steps.text: Stand the leg on the deck in the corner between the reel and the bay, foot along y. 4 x M3 x 10 down through the foot into the deck inserts.
steps.label: motor 113
steps.heading: Step 8 (motor 113): Motor leg

steps.title: Can stay
steps.text: Post against the plate's rear face, 2 x M3 x 12 into the plate inserts. Cable tie or hose clamp round the motor can through the two cradle slots, firm but not crushing.
steps.label: motor 114
steps.heading: Step 9 (motor 114): Can stay

steps.title: Shafts and trains (other subsystems)
steps.text: Now cad-drum (coupler on the wiper shaft, SW_INDEX block on this plate's front face inserts: drum step "Main shaft: index contact"), cad-launch (rail and aim housing) and then the rail bridge and reel head (cad-reel, cad-drum: D49, they ride the rail) go in. Follow their steps, then come back. Leave a flex loop for the head's wires across the pivot (about 10 conductors, 41 deg of pitch).
steps.label: motor 119
steps.heading: Step 10 (motor 119): Shafts and trains (other subsystems)

steps.title: Main shaft: coupler and limiter
steps.text: Push the coupler hub onto the wiper output shaft (flats in line) until it stops on the end of the flats; its lower end goes into the puck bore, just clear of the motor's output boss. Drop the M8 nut into the hub pocket onto the thread (it sits about 8 mm down the pocket) and tighten it with a 13 mm socket (1/4 inch drive). Slide the outer coupler over the hub, line up the holes, push a shear pin in (head outside, its flat facing the outboard end) and put a piece of tape round the coupler over the head. Print the pins lying on their flat (D44: shear across the layers). Keep the 5 spare pins with the base. A broken pin stub comes out with an M3 screw turned into it. Then slide the REEL gear onto the coupler journal (plain face first) and screw the retaining washer to the journal end (2 x M3 x 6): the gear must spin free.
steps.label: main_shaft 130
steps.heading: Step 11 (main_shaft 130): Main shaft: coupler and limiter

steps.title: Main shaft: index contact
steps.text: Press an M3 nut into the index block pocket, screw the index lever foot to the block (M3 x 12), thread an M3 x 6 into the lever boss, head toward the nut. Screw the block's flange to the motor plate front face with two M3 x 10 into the frame inserts, nub on the coupler cam (D49: SW_INDEX stays on the frame, never on the rail). Set the gap so the screw head touches the nut near the top of a bump (about 1.5 mm on a low part). Battery unplugged: nut to GND, screw to SW_INDEX.
steps.label: main_shaft 131
steps.heading: Step 12 (main_shaft 131): Main shaft: index contact

steps.title: Main shaft: stack
steps.text: Slide the collar onto the main shaft from the spigot end and push the shaft about 42 mm into the coupler socket. The shaft is held endwise later by the launch sleeve and the magnet cap.
steps.label: main_stack 140
steps.heading: Step 13 (main_stack 140): Main shaft: stack

steps.title: Main shaft: LAUNCH dog ring and magnet cap
steps.text: Fit the LAUNCH dog ring on the launch sleeve flange (sleeve lugs in the ring slots, 3 x M3 x 10 from the sleeve side into the ring) before the launch sleeve goes on the spigot (launcher steps). After the launcher: glue the AS5600 magnet into the cap, push the cap on the spigot end (flat to flat) and fit the M3 x 6 onto the flat.
steps.label: main_stack 141
steps.heading: Step 14 (main_stack 141): Main shaft: LAUNCH dog ring and magnet cap

steps.title: Launcher 1: print the parts
steps.text: All PLA unless named. PPA-CF: big gear, drive gear, launch sleeve, big gear pin, SW_SEATED plunger and pushrod, and the aim gears (sun, idler, output, bevel, worm, crank). Use each part's print orientation from the print sheet: the carriage body lies on its side across the bed diagonal; the stop springs print upside down at 100 percent infill (all perimeters); rail pieces lie on their largest flat face. 0.2 mm layers, 4 walls on every loaded part. Hardware (launcher and aim train): M3 screws 2 x 6, 3 x 8, 14 x 10, 23 x 12, 5 x 16, 12 x 20, 4 x 30, plus 4 x 10 for the aim housing to the deck (Aim 3); 10 M3 nuts, 1 M3 nyloc; M8 x 25 bolt and M8 nut; 2 x 608; 1 x 693ZZ (lip roller); 4 M3 heat-set inserts (rail rear flange for the reel head, D49); 2 x 8 mm steel rod pins (cut to the length on the print sheet) for the spring anchors; sprag #1 (CSK20PP); the two springs.
steps.label: launcher 190
steps.heading: Step 15 (launcher 190): Launcher 1: print the parts

steps.title: Launcher 2: join the rail
steps.text: Lay the rear, mid and front rail pieces in a line on a flat table. Push each joint together and fit 2 x M3 x 20 with nuts through each flange pair (8 in total). Tighten evenly; file any step inside the track where the pieces meet so the carriage shoes slide over it.
steps.label: launcher 191
warnings: launch_rail_front, launch_rail_mid, launch_rail_rear rest only on parts placed later (by 'Head frame on the rail', 'Launcher 2b: splice straps and aim lug', 'Launcher 3: big gear', 'Launcher 4: drive gear, sprag #1 and the launch sleeve' and 8 more)
steps.heading: Step 16 (launcher 191): Launcher 2: join the rail

steps.title: Launcher 2b: splice straps and aim lug
steps.text: Screw a splice strap on each wall top across the front joint (4 x M3 x 10 self tap each). Bolt the aim lug to the left rail wall now (2 x M3 x 12 self tap): the spring guards cover its screws later.
steps.label: launcher 192
steps.heading: Step 17 (launcher 192): Launcher 2b: splice straps and aim lug

steps.title: Launcher 3: big gear
steps.text: Hold the big gear between the two cheeks of the mid piece, the toothed sector towards the drum side (right) and the full ring of teeth towards the left, with the spacer washer between the gear and the left cheek. Push the big gear pin through cheek, gear, washer, cheek from the right and snap the C clip into its groove. The gear must spin freely with almost no end play.
steps.label: launcher 193
steps.heading: Step 18 (launcher 193): Launcher 3: big gear

steps.title: Launcher 4: drive gear, sprag #1 and the launch sleeve
steps.text: First bolt cad-drum's LAUNCH dog ring to the sleeve flange: lugs in the ring slots, 3 x M3 x 8 from the flange side into the tapped ring (the heads are out of reach once the sleeve is in the cheeks). Slide sprag #1 into the drive gear so its outer keyway takes the rib inside the gear. Check the direction: look at the gear from its collar side (the side that goes to the right, towards the motor), hold the gear and turn the inner race with a finger. It must turn freely counter-clockwise (BACKWARD) and lock clockwise (FORWARD: clockwise seen from the motor side is the cock direction). If it is the other way round, push the sprag out, turn it over and slide it in other face first. Hold the drive gear between the cheeks (collar side right, then the spacer washer on its left), meshing the big gear's full ring of teeth. Turn the cheek bores so their slots point down, then push the launch sleeve in from the motor side, outboard end first, ribs lined up with the slots and the sprag keyway, until the long (15 mm) rib sits inside the sprag.
steps.label: launcher 194
steps.heading: Step 19 (launcher 194): Launcher 4: drive gear, sprag #1 and the launch sleeve

steps.title: Launcher 5: carriage
steps.text: Turn the big gear so its toothless gap faces the rack. Slide the carriage BODY into the track from the FRONT end (the rear flange blocks the rear), rack teeth down, until its rear face reaches the stop position. Yoke: push the SW_SEATED pushrod into the block bore from the rear, collar first, then push the plunger's pin up through the block from below (pad under the left arm) and press the head cap on the pin top. Lower the yoke onto the carriage rear so its key plates drop into the slots in the body webs, and fit 1 x M3 x 10 per side through the yoke into the webs. Press a printed spring peg up into each inner (y 38) peg hole from below, flat to the rear, to the end of the hole.
steps.label: launcher 195
steps.heading: Step 20 (launcher 195): Launcher 5: carriage

steps.title: Fit the remaining launch parts
steps.text: Parts without an explicit assembly step: launch_dart.
steps.heading: Step 21: Fit the remaining launch parts

steps.title: Launcher 5b: lip roller
steps.text: Press a 693ZZ into the lip roller, put a printed thrust washer each side in its bore (hub to the bearing), drop roller and washers into the fork at the carriage front and fit the M3 x 16 and a nyloc nut; it must spin freely. The tether runs over it in tow and retrieval, and the dart's tail slides in over it through the funnel onto the cradle.
steps.label: launcher 196
steps.heading: Step 22 (launcher 196): Launcher 5b: lip roller

steps.title: Launcher 6: carriage stop frames
steps.text: For each side, before any spring: slide the stop frame onto the rail from the outboard side (it does not drop straight down past the inboard preload ledge). 2 x M3 x 12 through the rear foot into the rail wall, and 2 x M3 x 16 down through the front foot into the rail front plate, driven through the access holes in the frame's front wall.
steps.label: launcher 197
steps.heading: Step 23 (launcher 197): Launcher 6: carriage stop frames

steps.title: Launcher 6b: spring guards
steps.text: Screw the spring guard plates to the rail walls and anchor posts (M3 self tap into the pilots, see the print sheet), four per side: a (rear, with the end wall), b1 and b2 (either side of the stop frame's rear leg) and c (front, 2 x M3 x 12 into the front plate edge). Slide each one in from the side, under the stop frame's outboard bar. Wall brackets: M3 x 12 self tap, head and hex key through the hole in the plate; b2 foot: M3 x 10 down. Never cock with a guard off.
steps.label: launcher 198
steps.heading: Step 24 (launcher 198): Launcher 6b: spring guards

steps.title: Launcher 6c: stop springs
steps.text: Put each stop spring on its ledges inside its frame, rear bar towards the yoke arm, and pull it onto the frame's front wall with the 2 x M3 x 20 draw screws (heads on the front wall), a turn each in turn, until it sits on the wall (6.6 mm of preload). The rear bar must rest on both ledges.
steps.label: launcher 199
steps.heading: Step 25 (launcher 199): Launcher 6c: stop springs

steps.title: Launcher 7: contacts
steps.text: SW_HOME (right lip) and SW_SEATED (left lip): drop an M3 nut into the slot in the rail wall with a stripped wire end under it. Put a ring lug (or a stripped wire end wrapped once) on an M3 x 6 under its head and screw it up into the lever's boss, head down, until the tip is flush with the boss top (the pad beside it must stay the highest point), then screw the lever root to the lip with one M3 x 10 (self tap). Set the gap with the carriage pushed back at least 10 mm (lever free): turn the screw down until the head just touches the nut (meter beeps), then back it off ONE full turn (0.5 mm gap; a dab of nail varnish on the thread holds it). Carriage on its stop: the right foot presses the pad about 0.95 mm and SW_HOME must read closed; 2 mm back it must read open (if not, a quarter turn at a time). SW_SEATED closes only with a dart on the sled (no springs yet: hold the carriage on its stop by hand to check). SW_GAP, SW_RAIL_LOW and the AS5600 carrier are fitted in the Sensors steps (cad-sensors).
steps.label: launcher 200
steps.heading: Step 26 (launcher 200): Launcher 7: contacts

steps.title: Launcher 8: time the big gear (fingers clear)
steps.text: No springs fitted yet. Hold the carriage on its stop by hand and turn the drive gear FORWARD until the first tooth after the toothless gap just touches the rearmost rack tooth: this is HOME (SW_GAP is set to it in the Sensors steps). Turning on pulls the carriage back smoothly; at full cock the cut last tooth lets go (push the carriage home by hand). Hold the drive gear from the side and never put a hand in front of the carriage.
steps.label: launcher 201
steps.heading: Step 27 (launcher 201): Launcher 8: time the big gear (fingers clear)

steps.title: Aim 1: aim housing, worm, wheel, crank
steps.text: Build the aim housing on the bench (it goes onto the base later, after the rail). The AS5600 carrier and SW_RAIL_LOW are cad-sensors parts (Sensors steps), screwed into the pilots on the housing. Push the countershaft in from the inboard side through the inner wall bushing, through the big bevel (D bore, slid on from the outboard end of the shaft) and into the outer wall bushing. Drop the M8 nut into the hex pocket on the inner face of the outer wall, fit the two 608 bearings into the crank (worm wheel) hub, hold the crank in place and push the M8 x 25 bolt in from outboard through the wall, the nut and both bearings; tighten so the head and nut clamp the wall. Lay the worm shaft with the small bevel in its saddles and screw the cap on (4 x M3 x 30 self tap). The housing screws to the deck later (Aim 3), from the top: 4 x M3 x 10 down through the counterbored holes in its foot flanges (two behind the spine, one in front of the outer wall, one on the inboard tab) into the deck's heat-set inserts. The SW_RAIL_LOW bracket on the foot extension has its own deck screw (Sensors 2).
steps.label: aim 205
steps.heading: Step 28 (aim 205): Aim 1: aim housing, worm, wheel, crank

steps.title: Aim 2: splitter
steps.text: Slide the sun onto the sleeve's outer rib. On the bench: fit the idler on the swing arm pin and snap the printed C clip into the pin groove, and push the printed drag pad into the arm hub pocket with the shim behind its root block (a thicker shim gives more drag). Then slide the arm onto the sleeve next to the sun (there is no room to fit the idler once the arm is on).
steps.label: aim 206
steps.heading: Step 29 (aim 206): Aim 2: splitter

steps.title: Aim 3: lug, conrod, rail onto the base
steps.text: With the sun and swing arm already on the sleeve (the lug is on the rail since Launcher 2b), slide the rail assembly's sleeve along the main axis onto the drum's d12 spigot from the outboard side (the LAUNCH dog ring is already bolted to its flange, Launcher 4) until the ring's dogs sit by the drum collar. Hang the conrod's upper eye on the lug pin and snap a printed C clip into that groove. Then slide the aim housing on from the outboard side so the sleeve end enters its bushing and the crank pin enters the conrod's lower eye (hold the swing arm with the idler pointing down and a little to the rear, clear of the output gear, and let the arm go in between the two stop posts on the housing's inner face as they come up to it); snap a printed C clip onto the crank pin and screw the housing to the deck from the top: 4 x M3 x 10 through the counterbored foot flange holes into the deck inserts. Turn the sleeve backward by hand: the arm swings the idler into the output gear, comes to rest on its engaged stop post and drives the gear without binding; forward, the arm swings out onto the other post and the output gear stays still. Then turn the wiper backward slowly: the rail rises to 47 deg, then lowers to 6 deg.
steps.label: aim 207
steps.heading: Step 30 (aim 207): Aim 3: lug, conrod, rail onto the base

steps.title: Launcher 10: wiring (battery unplugged)
steps.text: Battery unplugged. Run the SW_HOME, SW_SEATED and SW_GAP wires along the rail to the pivot and leave a 150 mm loop at the main axis before they go to the frame. No wire goes onto the carriage. Each contact: one wire to its ESP32 pin (SW_HOME 21, SW_GAP 39, SW_RAIL_LOW 40, SW_SEATED 41, as params.SWITCHES), the other to GND.
steps.label: aim 208
steps.heading: Step 31 (aim 208): Launcher 10: wiring (battery unplugged)

steps.title: Sensors 1: build the two contact switches (SW_RAIL_LOW, SW_GAP)
steps.text: For each switch: press an M3 nut into the hex trap on the base pillar (a drop of glue), solder a wire to the nut through the side slot and lay it in the groove. Screw the lever onto the pad with 2 x M3x10 self tapping screws. Screw an M3x10 through the lever boss from the top, head down, with a ring lug and the second wire under a jam nut on top. Turn the screw until the head touches the nut, then back it off 1.9 turns (gap about 0.9 mm, 0.5 mm per turn) and lock the jam nut.
steps.label: sensors 210
steps.heading: Step 32 (sensors 210): Sensors 1: build the two contact switches (SW_RAIL_LOW, SW_GAP)

steps.title: Sensors 2: SW_RAIL_LOW on the aim housing
steps.text: Screw the switch base to its bracket (4 x M3x8 self tapping), lever pointing to the crank. Set the bracket foot on the housing foot extension in front of the crank. Screw it down with an M3x10 in the hole nearest the crank (self taps into the housing) and an M3x16 in the counterbored hole at the front end of the foot: down through the foot and the foot extension into the deck insert under it (the bracket's own deck screw). Turn the crank by hand (wiper backwards) to the lowest rail position: the cam lobe presses the lever tip and the meter shows the switch closed. Turn the crank about 20 deg either side: the switch must open.
steps.label: sensors 211
steps.heading: Step 33 (sensors 211): Sensors 2: SW_RAIL_LOW on the aim housing

steps.title: Sensors 3: SW_GAP on the right rail cheek
steps.text: Build SW_GAP as in Sensors 1 (its base has its own arm). Hold the arm tab on the outer face of the right rail cheek, below the big gear, and screw it on with 2 x M3x12 (heads in the counterbores). With the big gear at rest (toothless gap at the rack) the cam bump presses the lever: switch closed. Turn the gear 20 deg either way: switch open.
steps.label: sensors 212
steps.heading: Step 34 (sensors 212): Sensors 3: SW_GAP on the right rail cheek

steps.title: Sensors 4: AS5600 board
steps.text: Do this after the magnet cap is on the main shaft end (drum steps): the board sits 2 mm in front of it. Battery unplugged. Plug the STEMMA QT cable into the board's connector on the +x end (the end away from the housing spine). Push the board onto the 4 pegs of the carrier, chip facing out. Drop an M3 nut into each hex pocket in the carrier back, lay the strips over the board edges (pegs through their holes) and screw each from the strip front with an M3x12 into its nut. Screw the carrier column to the aim housing spine with 2 x M3x16. Check by eye: the chip sits on the shaft axis, about 2.0 mm from the magnet face, and the cap turns free.
steps.label: sensors 213
steps.heading: Step 35 (sensors 213): Sensors 4: AS5600 board

steps.title: Reel bridge on rail cheek A
steps.text: Press the 8 mm c1' stub into its hole in the bridge plate. Press the CSK20PP into the sprag hub (key slot on the printed rib; seen from the outboard side the inner ring must turn freely counter-clockwise and lock clockwise) and screw the hub to the plate's outboard face with four M3 x 16. Hold the bridge inboard of the main shaft stack, below the REEL gear, and bolt its box arm to the inner face of rail cheek A with two M3 x 16 (heads reached through the two holes in the arm).
steps.label: bridge 220
steps.heading: Step 36 (bridge 220): Reel bridge on rail cheek A

steps.title: Countershaft C, C1 and bevel B1
steps.text: Slide countershaft C into the sprag from the outboard side, key rib in the keyway, until its collar meets the plate. Slide C1 (49 teeth) onto the D-flat so it meshes the REEL gear, then the 24-tooth bevel, teeth outboard. Turn the REEL gear by hand: C1 turns one way only (the sprag holds the other).
steps.label: bridge 221
steps.heading: Step 37 (bridge 221): Countershaft C, C1 and bevel B1

steps.title: Take-up gears on the bridge
steps.text: Slide c1' (46 teeth) onto the stub, hub outboard, meshing the bus gear. Clip the swing arm's split ring over c1's hub and put the 30-tooth swing idler on the arm pin. Push countershaft T into its bushing and slide T1 (20 teeth) and the B2 bevel onto its flat. Turn the wiper forward by hand: the idler swings into T1; backward it swings out.
steps.label: bridge 222
steps.heading: Step 38 (bridge 222): Take-up gears on the bridge

steps.title: Shafts along the rail
steps.text: Slide the 12-tooth B1 pinion onto the front flat of u-shaft C and feed the shaft rearward through the bridge block until the pinion meshes the B1 bevel. Slide the B2 pinion onto the front flat of u-shaft T and feed it rearward through the bridge pillar until the pinion meshes B2. Both shafts reach back to the reel head.
steps.label: bridge 223
steps.heading: Step 39 (bridge 223): Shafts along the rail

steps.title: Bridge: shift rail, fork, bell crank and dog contacts
steps.text: Press the shift rail into the bridge plate boss (flat facing the rail). Press an M3 nut into the hex hole of the fork's tab. Thread an M3 x 8 into each dog post boss, heads toward each other. Slide the fork sleeve onto the rail with the yoke under the collar and drop the yoke pads into the collar groove, then slide the dog post onto the rail end and tighten its clamp screw (M3 x 8, tapped) on the rail flat. Put the bell crank on the shelf with its pin up in the fork lug's slot and fit the M3 x 16 pivot screw (tapped into the shelf, the crank must swing). Battery unplugged: nut wire to GND, REEL side screw to SW_DOG_R, LAUNCH side screw to SW_DOG_L; the wires run in the flex loop to the frame.
steps.label: bridge 224
warnings: drum_crank rest only on parts placed later (by 'Link from the follower to the bell crank')
steps.heading: Step 40 (bridge 224): Bridge: shift rail, fork, bell crank and dog contacts

steps.title: Head frame on the rail
steps.text: Screw the front plate to the spine (three M3 x 12 through the spine into the plate). Slide the front plate's bushing over the rear end of u-shaft T and bolt the plate to the rail's rear flange with four M3 x 16 into the flange inserts. Screw the mid plate to the front plate (M3 x 12).
steps.label: head 225
steps.heading: Step 41 (head 225): Head frame on the rail

steps.title: Spool, shaft and clutch
steps.text: Press a 608 into each end of the spool. Push the line end through the small hole near the inboard flange, knot it inside (figure eight) and wind 20 m on (line over the top, leaving toward the rail). Slide the clutch disk onto the outboard flat of the spool shaft (friction ring inboard), then from the other end the spool until its outboard face meets the disk, then the thrust ring, boss toward the spool. Feed the inboard end through the mid plate bushing and slide the B3 bevel onto its flat. Slide the B3 bevel for u-shaft T onto the shaft's rear flat; the two bevels mesh.
steps.label: head 226
steps.heading: Step 42 (head 226): Spool, shaft and clutch

steps.title: Capstan tube, drum, cup shaft and cup
steps.text: Slide the capstan drum onto the front end of the capstan tube, key slot on the rib. Push the cup shaft through the tube from the front (neck end in front), slide the cup onto it (flat in the bore onto the flat, eyelet lug at the bottom, in line with the spool) and push Harry's small C-clip onto the neck.
steps.label: head 227
warnings: reel_c, reel_cup, reel_cup_clip, reel_drum, reel_k rest only on parts placed later (by 'P1, the capstan gears and the clutch lever', 'P1b, cup gear and P2')
steps.heading: Step 43 (head 227): Capstan tube, drum, cup shaft and cup

steps.title: P1, the capstan gears and the clutch lever
steps.text: Press the G_b axle (8 mm rod, 26 long) into P1. Slide P1 over the capstan tube, the rear end of u-shaft C and the spool shaft end (its leg), and screw it to the spine (two M3 x 12) and to the mid plate. Put G_c (23 teeth) on the tube flat, G_a (26) on u-shaft C's flat and G_b (32) on its axle. Hang the clutch lever on the P1 post with the M3 x 16 pivot screw (it must swing), its upper arm under the drum's brake cam, the FIRM screw toward the thrust ring. Screw the LIGHT stop screw into P1 under the upper arm.
steps.label: head 228
steps.heading: Step 44 (head 228): P1, the capstan gears and the clutch lever

steps.title: Head: drum, guide rod and follower
steps.text: Press the drum axle and the follower guide rod into the reel head front plate (flats as on the print sheet). Slide drum A onto the axle, gear first, then the follower onto the rod with its pin in drum A's groove, then drum B (hex socket over the spigot; it fits one way only). Press bracket B onto the axle and rod ends with the wrap idler shaft in its journal and screw the bracket's foot to the spine (2 x M3 x 12 from outside the spine).
steps.label: head 229
steps.heading: Step 45 (head 229): Head: drum, guide rod and follower

steps.title: Head: wrap idler
steps.text: Push the 49-tooth output gear onto the idler shaft's flat (D bore). Feed the shaft into bracket B from the front so the small pinion sits at the drum's segment teeth and the lock cam over the lock ring; its rear journal goes into P2 when P2 goes on. Turn the drum to LAUNCH: the flat-sided lock cam must sit in the drum lock ring and the idler can no longer turn by hand.
steps.label: head 230
steps.heading: Step 46 (head 230): Head: wrap idler

steps.title: Head: N20
steps.text: Press the pinion onto the N20 output shaft (flat to flat) leaving 1.5 mm of shaft below it (that end runs in the front plate slot). Slide the N20 into the cradle from the open end, fit the end plate (2 x M3 x 8). Press an M3 nut into the pocket in the front plate's rear face, wire along its groove. Screw the cradle to the front plate: pivot screw M3 x 12 through the round hole, swing screw M3 x 12 through the arc slot at its full-mesh end, both tapped. Turn the SW_N20 screw (M3 x 8, tapped in the cradle plate) in until its tip just touches the nut. Strap the N20 body to the cradle with a cable tie (it rides the rail and sees every shot). Battery unplugged: nut to GND, screw to SW_N20.
steps.label: head 231
steps.heading: Step 47 (head 231): Head: N20

steps.title: P1b, cup gear and P2
steps.text: Fit P1b over the rear end of the capstan tube and screw it to the two P1 posts (M3 x 12). Slide the cup gear G_k (28 teeth, raised track forward) onto the cup shaft flat so it meshes the drum's wrap idler output with the cup at home (eyelet at the bottom). Screw P2 to the spine over the cup shaft and wrap idler ends (two M3 x 12). The cup must turn freely both ways.
steps.label: head 232
steps.heading: Step 48 (head 232): P1b, cup gear and P2

steps.title: SW_ARM contact
steps.text: Battery unplugged. Build the printed contact (see the contact switch page): nut pressed in the base trap, lever screwed onto the pad with 2 x M3 x 10 self tapping screws, M3 x 10 contact screw with its jam nut in the lever. Screw the base to P1b's rear face with four M3 x 10. SW_ARM is closed while the cup is away from home and opens at home: the lever rides the raised track on the front of the cup gear and drops into its notch at home. Cup at home: turn the contact screw until its head just touches the nut, back it off 1.9 turns (gap about 0.9 mm) and lock the jam nut. Check with the meter: about 15 degrees of cup turn either way closes it; at home it must be open.
steps.label: head 233
steps.heading: Step 49 (head 233): SW_ARM contact

steps.title: Shroud, line and clutch setting
steps.text: Put the shroud round the spool, open side at the top toward the rail, and screw its tab to the P1 leg (M3 x 8). Lead the line from the top of the spool straight forward under the capstan drum and through the cup eyelet from behind, then forward through the pusher hole to the dart's tail cap. Wind 20 m through the eyelet once on the bench before the first shot (D49: the pack mounds in the middle). Set LIGHT with the drum at LAUNCH: turn the LIGHT stop screw until a 25 g weight hung on the line end just pulls line off slowly (0.25 N). Set FIRM with the drum at NEUTRAL: turn the FIRM screw until the line slips at 5.0 N on the luggage scale, then lock its nut.
steps.label: head 234
steps.heading: Step 50 (head 234): Shroud, line and clutch setting

steps.title: Head: code switches
steps.text: Press an M3 nut into each of the 3 pockets of the switch block and screw its foot to the spine (2 x M3 x 12 from outside the spine). Screw each lever foot to the block (M3 x 12), nub on its band. Thread an M3 x 6 into each lever boss, head toward the nut, so the head touches the nut near the top of a bump (gap about 1.8 mm with the nub low). Battery unplugged: nuts to GND, screws to SW_DRUM_A (nearest the drum gear), SW_DRUM_B, SW_DRUM_C.
steps.label: head 235
steps.heading: Step 51 (head 235): Head: code switches

steps.title: Link from the follower to the bell crank
steps.text: Cut the 8 mm steel rod to the length on the print sheet, deburr the ends and press a printed eye onto each end, both eye holes parallel. Pass the rod through the window in the head front plate, screw the top eye to the follower lug and the bottom eye to the bell crank's input arm (M3 x 16 and nyloc nut each, snug: the eyes must swing). Turn the drum by hand from LAUNCH to REEL: the follower slides 14 mm, the crank turns and the collar moves from the LAUNCH dogs to the REEL dogs.
steps.label: head 236
steps.heading: Step 52 (head 236): Link from the follower to the bell crank

steps.title: Electronics bay
steps.text: Battery unplugged. Bay on the deck, 4 x M3 x 10 through the tabs. Boards in: BTS7960 on its 4 standoffs (M3 x 6), heatsink down; ESP32 DevKitC pins down into the cradle, USB end into the wall slot, clamp with 2 x M3 x 8; DRV8833, MP1584 and HX711 into their pockets with a cable tie through the floor slots or a drop of hot glue. Fuse holder in its cradle with a cable tie.
steps.label: electronics 240
steps.heading: Step 53 (electronics 240): Electronics bay

steps.title: Set the buck BEFORE wiring the DRV8833
steps.text: Battery unplugged. Wire only the buck input to the fuse output and ground. Plug the battery in, meter on the buck output, turn the trimpot until it reads 9.0 V. Unplug the battery. Only then wire buck output to DRV8833 VIN (the DRV8833 dies above 10.8 V).
steps.label: electronics 241
steps.heading: Step 54 (electronics 241): Set the buck BEFORE wiring the DRV8833

steps.title: Camera, receiver and cable anchors
steps.text: Camera column on the deck, 4 x M3 x 10 into the inserts. Clip the Kiyo X onto the 16 mm edge plate like onto a monitor (or use a 1/4-20 tripod screw up through the plate hole); it looks forward along the launch line. RC832: stand it antenna-end up in its holder slot, leads out of the low notch, holder 2 x M3 x 10. Cable anchors 1 x M3 x 12 each; tie the camera USB, the receiver AV lead and the capture dongle lead to them so no plug carries the cable weight.
steps.label: electronics 242
steps.heading: Step 55 (electronics 242): Camera, receiver and cable anchors

steps.title: Wiring and lid
steps.text: Battery unplugged. Follow firmware/base/WIRING.md. Every wire leaving the bay goes through its wall exit and is cable-tied to the anchor beside it (strain relief). 14 AWG for battery, fuse, BTS7960 and motor. Lid on, 4 x M3 x 6. USB cable from the ESP32 native USB port to the Jetson.
steps.label: electronics 243
steps.heading: Step 56 (electronics 243): Wiring and lid

steps.title: Gear guards
steps.text: After every train has been turned by hand: the hood goes over the gears in front of the motor plate, M3 x 10 through each lug into the plate inserts; the front guard stands on the deck between the drum gears and the bay, M3 x 10 into the deck inserts. Turn the wiper by hand once: nothing rubs.
steps.label: guards 250
steps.heading: Step 57 (guards 250): Gear guards

steps.title: Test stage 5 only: springs (NOT during assembly)
steps.text: The springs go on at test stage 5, after the big gear timing, the contacts and the aim train have been checked without them. Spring guards on first (never cock with a guard off) and never fire without the tether attached (D11). Hook the back end of each spring over the inner peg of the yoke arm. Put the front hook between post and strap, lined up with the main hole, and push the 8 mm steel rod pin down through strap, hook and post. Hole set F, 8.5 mm rearward, is the fallback if the hang test shows the spring needs less stretch. The outer holes are spare. The springs are slightly stretched and hold the carriage against the stop. A drop of glue on the pin top stops it working up.
steps.label: test_stage_only 999
steps.heading: Step 58 (test_stage_only 999): Test stage 5 only: springs (NOT during assembly)

TIMELINE: load
Dart seated on the sled, drum in LAUNCH, rail low, line taut.
aim
Wiper backward: the crank-rocker lifts the rail and the reel head on it to 36 deg; the worm holds it.
cock
Wiper forward: the big gear draws the sled back 241 mm; the take-up winds the slack.
fire
The relieved tooth lets go: the sled throws the dart; the big gear resets into its gap.
flight
Dart in flight; the line pays straight off the free spool through the cup eyelet against the 0.25 N clutch.
rail_low
D45: wiper backward through the rest of the aim cycle: the rail comes down to 6 deg before the wrap, so tow tension cannot push the carriage back.
neutral
Unload jog, then the drum goes to NEUTRAL: wiper coupled to nothing.
wrap
Right after landing, while the line still lies slack: the drum turns the wrap cup 7 times round the capstan.
wrapped
Drum to the WRAPPED park (314): cup locked, clutch FIRM, collar still NEUTRAL.
anchor
The dart plants its foot and screws its two drills into the ground.
tidy
Wiper forward: the take-up pulls the slack through the free capstan until the line is straight.
reel_engage
Drum into REEL while the wiper creeps forward: the collar drops into the REEL dogs.
tow
Capstan winches the rover toward the anchored dart; sprag #2 holds the load.
release
The base stops (the worm holds the line), then the dart unscrews its drills and lets go.
reel_in
Capstan reels the dart in until about 1.5 m remain.
unload
Wiper jogs 6 deg back inside the dog window, then the drum goes back to the WRAPPED park (314): the collar leaves the REEL dogs.
unwrap
Drum from the park back through the wrap sector to 62, collar in NEUTRAL; the wiper turns forward slowly and the take-up winds the freed line.
approach
Drum to NEUTRAL; the FIRM take-up pulls the dart tail first onto the sled until SW_SEATED.
to_launch
Drum to LAUNCH: clutch LIGHT, collar into the LAUNCH dogs (a 2 deg alignment creep). Rail already low: ready to aim again.

steps_authored.title: Main shaft: coupler and limiter
steps_authored.text: Push the coupler hub onto the wiper output shaft (flats in line) until it stops on the end of the flats; its lower end goes into the puck bore, just clear of the motor's output boss. Drop the M8 nut into the hub pocket onto the thread (it sits about 8 mm down the pocket) and tighten it with a 13 mm socket (1/4 inch drive). Slide the outer coupler over the hub, line up the holes, push a shear pin in (head outside, its flat facing the outboard end) and put a piece of tape round the coupler over the head. Print the pins lying on their flat (D44: shear across the layers). Keep the 5 spare pins with the base. A broken pin stub comes out with an M3 screw turned into it. Then slide the REEL gear onto the coupler journal (plain face first) and screw the retaining washer to the journal end (2 x M3 x 6): the gear must spin free.

steps_authored.title: Main shaft: index contact
steps_authored.text: Press an M3 nut into the index block pocket, screw the index lever foot to the block (M3 x 12), thread an M3 x 6 into the lever boss, head toward the nut. Screw the block's flange to the motor plate front face with two M3 x 10 into the frame inserts, nub on the coupler cam (D49: SW_INDEX stays on the frame, never on the rail). Set the gap so the screw head touches the nut near the top of a bump (about 1.5 mm on a low part). Battery unplugged: nut to GND, screw to SW_INDEX.

steps_authored.title: Main shaft: stack
steps_authored.text: Slide the collar onto the main shaft from the spigot end and push the shaft about 42 mm into the coupler socket. The shaft is held endwise later by the launch sleeve and the magnet cap.

steps_authored.title: Main shaft: LAUNCH dog ring and magnet cap
steps_authored.text: Fit the LAUNCH dog ring on the launch sleeve flange (sleeve lugs in the ring slots, 3 x M3 x 10 from the sleeve side into the ring) before the launch sleeve goes on the spigot (launcher steps). After the launcher: glue the AS5600 magnet into the cap, push the cap on the spigot end (flat to flat) and fit the M3 x 6 onto the flat.

steps_authored.title: Bridge: shift rail, fork, bell crank and dog contacts
steps_authored.text: Press the shift rail into the bridge plate boss (flat facing the rail). Press an M3 nut into the hex hole of the fork's tab. Thread an M3 x 8 into each dog post boss, heads toward each other. Slide the fork sleeve onto the rail with the yoke under the collar and drop the yoke pads into the collar groove, then slide the dog post onto the rail end and tighten its clamp screw (M3 x 8, tapped) on the rail flat. Put the bell crank on the shelf with its pin up in the fork lug's slot and fit the M3 x 16 pivot screw (tapped into the shelf, the crank must swing). Battery unplugged: nut wire to GND, REEL side screw to SW_DOG_R, LAUNCH side screw to SW_DOG_L; the wires run in the flex loop to the frame.

steps_authored.title: Head: drum, guide rod and follower
steps_authored.text: Press the drum axle and the follower guide rod into the reel head front plate (flats as on the print sheet). Slide drum A onto the axle, gear first, then the follower onto the rod with its pin in drum A's groove, then drum B (hex socket over the spigot; it fits one way only). Press bracket B onto the axle and rod ends with the wrap idler shaft in its journal and screw the bracket's foot to the spine (2 x M3 x 12 from outside the spine).

steps_authored.title: Head: wrap idler
steps_authored.text: Push the 49-tooth output gear onto the idler shaft's flat (D bore). Feed the shaft into bracket B from the front so the small pinion sits at the drum's segment teeth and the lock cam over the lock ring; its rear journal goes into P2 when P2 goes on. Turn the drum to LAUNCH: the flat-sided lock cam must sit in the drum lock ring and the idler can no longer turn by hand.

steps_authored.title: Head: N20
steps_authored.text: Press the pinion onto the N20 output shaft (flat to flat) leaving 1.5 mm of shaft below it (that end runs in the front plate slot). Slide the N20 into the cradle from the open end, fit the end plate (2 x M3 x 8). Press an M3 nut into the pocket in the front plate's rear face, wire along its groove. Screw the cradle to the front plate: pivot screw M3 x 12 through the round hole, swing screw M3 x 12 through the arc slot at its full-mesh end, both tapped. Turn the SW_N20 screw (M3 x 8, tapped in the cradle plate) in until its tip just touches the nut. Strap the N20 body to the cradle with a cable tie (it rides the rail and sees every shot). Battery unplugged: nut to GND, screw to SW_N20.

steps_authored.title: Head: code switches
steps_authored.text: Press an M3 nut into each of the 3 pockets of the switch block and screw its foot to the spine (2 x M3 x 12 from outside the spine). Screw each lever foot to the block (M3 x 12), nub on its band. Thread an M3 x 6 into each lever boss, head toward the nut, so the head touches the nut near the top of a bump (gap about 1.8 mm with the nub low). Battery unplugged: nuts to GND, screws to SW_DRUM_A (nearest the drum gear), SW_DRUM_B, SW_DRUM_C.

steps_authored.title: Link from the follower to the bell crank
steps_authored.text: Cut the 8 mm steel rod to the length on the print sheet, deburr the ends and press a printed eye onto each end, both eye holes parallel. Pass the rod through the window in the head front plate, screw the top eye to the follower lug and the bottom eye to the bell crank's input arm (M3 x 16 and nyloc nut each, snug: the eyes must swing). Turn the drum by hand from LAUNCH to REEL: the follower slides 14 mm, the crank turns and the collar moves from the LAUNCH dogs to the REEL dogs.

steps_authored.title: Heat-set inserts
steps_authored.text: Soldering iron with an insert tip, about 220 C for PLA and about 280 C for the PPA-CF puck. Press every M3 x 4 x 5 insert square into its 4.0 mm hole until flush: deck (24), motor plate (2 for the leg bridge, 2 for the can stay, 3 for the gear hood), puck adapter (8 in the rear lip, 2 on the front face for cad-drum's SW_INDEX block), bay (corner bosses, standoffs, clamp posts, perfboard bosses). Let each cool before the next one nearby.

steps_authored.title: Drill the rover
steps_authored.text: Lay the deck on the rover top plate where it will live (launch direction forward). Mark through the 45 perimeter holes with a 3 mm drill or a scriber (or tape down the 1:1 PDF template from cad/parts/_frame_tests/drill_template.py), take the deck off, drill 3.4 mm. Deburr.

steps_authored.title: Deck on the rover
steps_authored.text: Slide the tiles together on the dovetails (from above). M3 x 25 SHCS down through every perimeter hole, washer and nyloc under the rover plate. Snug, not crushed. Do this before the other subsystems put their feet down: some rover bolts sit under their feet.

steps_authored.title: Motor leg
steps_authored.text: Stand the leg on the deck in the corner between the reel and the bay, foot along y. 4 x M3 x 10 down through the foot into the deck inserts.

steps_authored.title: Motor plate
steps_authored.text: Hold the motor plate upright (front face, the side without the bridge, towards +y) with its bridge against the top of the leg. 2 x M3 x 12 along y through the leg's long counterbores into the bridge inserts.

steps_authored.title: Wiper motor on the puck (bench)
steps_authored.text: Battery unplugged. Put the M6 bolts through the puck slots from the front (heads sit in the slot counterbores), into the motor bosses (threaded bosses, or a nut behind each boss ear). Slide the motor so its shaft is centred in the bore (a 10 mm drill shank in the coupler bore helps), then tighten.

steps_authored.title: Puck into the plate
steps_authored.text: Feed the puck into the plate window from behind (the motor side) until its lip sits on the plate's rear face. From the front, M3 x 12 through the plate into the lip inserts (8 of the 8 rim holes have both plate and lip; use those).

steps_authored.title: Can stay
steps_authored.text: Post against the plate's rear face, 2 x M3 x 12 into the plate inserts. Cable tie or hose clamp round the motor can through the two cradle slots, firm but not crushing.

steps_authored.title: Shafts and trains (other subsystems)
steps_authored.text: Now cad-drum (coupler on the wiper shaft, SW_INDEX block on this plate's front face inserts: drum step "Main shaft: index contact"), cad-launch (rail and aim housing) and then the rail bridge and reel head (cad-reel, cad-drum: D49, they ride the rail) go in. Follow their steps, then come back. Leave a flex loop for the head's wires across the pivot (about 10 conductors, 41 deg of pitch).

steps_authored.title: Gear guards
steps_authored.text: After every train has been turned by hand: the hood goes over the gears in front of the motor plate, M3 x 10 through each lug into the plate inserts; the front guard stands on the deck between the drum gears and the bay, M3 x 10 into the deck inserts. Turn the wiper by hand once: nothing rubs.

steps_authored.title: Electronics bay
steps_authored.text: Battery unplugged. Bay on the deck, 4 x M3 x 10 through the tabs. Boards in: BTS7960 on its 4 standoffs (M3 x 6), heatsink down; ESP32 DevKitC pins down into the cradle, USB end into the wall slot, clamp with 2 x M3 x 8; DRV8833, MP1584 and HX711 into their pockets with a cable tie through the floor slots or a drop of hot glue. Fuse holder in its cradle with a cable tie.

steps_authored.title: Set the buck BEFORE wiring the DRV8833
steps_authored.text: Battery unplugged. Wire only the buck input to the fuse output and ground. Plug the battery in, meter on the buck output, turn the trimpot until it reads 9.0 V. Unplug the battery. Only then wire buck output to DRV8833 VIN (the DRV8833 dies above 10.8 V).

steps_authored.title: Camera, receiver and cable anchors
steps_authored.text: Camera column on the deck, 4 x M3 x 10 into the inserts. Clip the Kiyo X onto the 16 mm edge plate like onto a monitor (or use a 1/4-20 tripod screw up through the plate hole); it looks forward along the launch line. RC832: stand it antenna-end up in its holder slot, leads out of the low notch, holder 2 x M3 x 10. Cable anchors 1 x M3 x 12 each; tie the camera USB, the receiver AV lead and the capture dongle lead to them so no plug carries the cable weight.

steps_authored.title: Wiring and lid
steps_authored.text: Battery unplugged. Follow firmware/base/WIRING.md. Every wire leaving the bay goes through its wall exit and is cable-tied to the anchor beside it (strain relief). 14 AWG for battery, fuse, BTS7960 and motor. Lid on, 4 x M3 x 6. USB cable from the ESP32 native USB port to the Jetson.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 1: print the parts
steps_authored.text: All PLA unless named. PPA-CF: big gear, drive gear, launch sleeve, big gear pin, SW_SEATED plunger and pushrod, and the aim gears (sun, idler, output, bevel, worm, crank). Use each part's print orientation from the print sheet: the carriage body lies on its side across the bed diagonal; the stop springs print upside down at 100 percent infill (all perimeters); rail pieces lie on their largest flat face. 0.2 mm layers, 4 walls on every loaded part. Hardware (launcher and aim train): M3 screws 2 x 6, 3 x 8, 14 x 10, 23 x 12, 5 x 16, 12 x 20, 4 x 30, plus 4 x 10 for the aim housing to the deck (Aim 3); 10 M3 nuts, 1 M3 nyloc; M8 x 25 bolt and M8 nut; 2 x 608; 1 x 693ZZ (lip roller); 4 M3 heat-set inserts (rail rear flange for the reel head, D49); 2 x 8 mm steel rod pins (cut to the length on the print sheet) for the spring anchors; sprag #1 (CSK20PP); the two springs.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 2: join the rail
steps_authored.text: Lay the rear, mid and front rail pieces in a line on a flat table. Push each joint together and fit 2 x M3 x 20 with nuts through each flange pair (8 in total). Tighten evenly; file any step inside the track where the pieces meet so the carriage shoes slide over it.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 2b: splice straps and aim lug
steps_authored.text: Screw a splice strap on each wall top across the front joint (4 x M3 x 10 self tap each). Bolt the aim lug to the left rail wall now (2 x M3 x 12 self tap): the spring guards cover its screws later.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 3: big gear
steps_authored.text: Hold the big gear between the two cheeks of the mid piece, the toothed sector towards the drum side (right) and the full ring of teeth towards the left, with the spacer washer between the gear and the left cheek. Push the big gear pin through cheek, gear, washer, cheek from the right and snap the C clip into its groove. The gear must spin freely with almost no end play.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 4: drive gear, sprag #1 and the launch sleeve
steps_authored.text: First bolt cad-drum's LAUNCH dog ring to the sleeve flange: lugs in the ring slots, 3 x M3 x 8 from the flange side into the tapped ring (the heads are out of reach once the sleeve is in the cheeks). Slide sprag #1 into the drive gear so its outer keyway takes the rib inside the gear. Check the direction: look at the gear from its collar side (the side that goes to the right, towards the motor), hold the gear and turn the inner race with a finger. It must turn freely counter-clockwise (BACKWARD) and lock clockwise (FORWARD: clockwise seen from the motor side is the cock direction). If it is the other way round, push the sprag out, turn it over and slide it in other face first. Hold the drive gear between the cheeks (collar side right, then the spacer washer on its left), meshing the big gear's full ring of teeth. Turn the cheek bores so their slots point down, then push the launch sleeve in from the motor side, outboard end first, ribs lined up with the slots and the sprag keyway, until the long (15 mm) rib sits inside the sprag.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 5: carriage
steps_authored.text: Turn the big gear so its toothless gap faces the rack. Slide the carriage BODY into the track from the FRONT end (the rear flange blocks the rear), rack teeth down, until its rear face reaches the stop position. Yoke: push the SW_SEATED pushrod into the block bore from the rear, collar first, then push the plunger's pin up through the block from below (pad under the left arm) and press the head cap on the pin top. Lower the yoke onto the carriage rear so its key plates drop into the slots in the body webs, and fit 1 x M3 x 10 per side through the yoke into the webs. Press a printed spring peg up into each inner (y 38) peg hole from below, flat to the rear, to the end of the hole.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 5b: lip roller
steps_authored.text: Press a 693ZZ into the lip roller, put a printed thrust washer each side in its bore (hub to the bearing), drop roller and washers into the fork at the carriage front and fit the M3 x 16 and a nyloc nut; it must spin freely. The tether runs over it in tow and retrieval, and the dart's tail slides in over it through the funnel onto the cradle.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 6: carriage stop frames
steps_authored.text: For each side, before any spring: slide the stop frame onto the rail from the outboard side (it does not drop straight down past the inboard preload ledge). 2 x M3 x 12 through the rear foot into the rail wall, and 2 x M3 x 16 down through the front foot into the rail front plate, driven through the access holes in the frame's front wall.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 6b: spring guards
steps_authored.text: Screw the spring guard plates to the rail walls and anchor posts (M3 self tap into the pilots, see the print sheet), four per side: a (rear, with the end wall), b1 and b2 (either side of the stop frame's rear leg) and c (front, 2 x M3 x 12 into the front plate edge). Slide each one in from the side, under the stop frame's outboard bar. Wall brackets: M3 x 12 self tap, head and hex key through the hole in the plate; b2 foot: M3 x 10 down. Never cock with a guard off.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 6c: stop springs
steps_authored.text: Put each stop spring on its ledges inside its frame, rear bar towards the yoke arm, and pull it onto the frame's front wall with the 2 x M3 x 20 draw screws (heads on the front wall), a turn each in turn, until it sits on the wall (6.6 mm of preload). The rear bar must rest on both ledges.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 7: contacts
steps_authored.text: SW_HOME (right lip) and SW_SEATED (left lip): drop an M3 nut into the slot in the rail wall with a stripped wire end under it. Put a ring lug (or a stripped wire end wrapped once) on an M3 x 6 under its head and screw it up into the lever's boss, head down, until the tip is flush with the boss top (the pad beside it must stay the highest point), then screw the lever root to the lip with one M3 x 10 (self tap). Set the gap with the carriage pushed back at least 10 mm (lever free): turn the screw down until the head just touches the nut (meter beeps), then back it off ONE full turn (0.5 mm gap; a dab of nail varnish on the thread holds it). Carriage on its stop: the right foot presses the pad about 0.95 mm and SW_HOME must read closed; 2 mm back it must read open (if not, a quarter turn at a time). SW_SEATED closes only with a dart on the sled (no springs yet: hold the carriage on its stop by hand to check). SW_GAP, SW_RAIL_LOW and the AS5600 carrier are fitted in the Sensors steps (cad-sensors).

steps_authored.title: Launcher 8: time the big gear (fingers clear)
steps_authored.text: No springs fitted yet. Hold the carriage on its stop by hand and turn the drive gear FORWARD until the first tooth after the toothless gap just touches the rearmost rack tooth: this is HOME (SW_GAP is set to it in the Sensors steps). Turning on pulls the carriage back smoothly; at full cock the cut last tooth lets go (push the carriage home by hand). Hold the drive gear from the side and never put a hand in front of the carriage.

steps_authored.title: Aim 1: aim housing, worm, wheel, crank
steps_authored.text: Build the aim housing on the bench (it goes onto the base later, after the rail). The AS5600 carrier and SW_RAIL_LOW are cad-sensors parts (Sensors steps), screwed into the pilots on the housing. Push the countershaft in from the inboard side through the inner wall bushing, through the big bevel (D bore, slid on from the outboard end of the shaft) and into the outer wall bushing. Drop the M8 nut into the hex pocket on the inner face of the outer wall, fit the two 608 bearings into the crank (worm wheel) hub, hold the crank in place and push the M8 x 25 bolt in from outboard through the wall, the nut and both bearings; tighten so the head and nut clamp the wall. Lay the worm shaft with the small bevel in its saddles and screw the cap on (4 x M3 x 30 self tap). The housing screws to the deck later (Aim 3), from the top: 4 x M3 x 10 down through the counterbored holes in its foot flanges (two behind the spine, one in front of the outer wall, one on the inboard tab) into the deck's heat-set inserts. The SW_RAIL_LOW bracket on the foot extension has its own deck screw (Sensors 2).

steps_authored.title: Aim 2: splitter
steps_authored.text: Slide the sun onto the sleeve's outer rib. On the bench: fit the idler on the swing arm pin and snap the printed C clip into the pin groove, and push the printed drag pad into the arm hub pocket with the shim behind its root block (a thicker shim gives more drag). Then slide the arm onto the sleeve next to the sun (there is no room to fit the idler once the arm is on).

steps_authored.title: Aim 3: lug, conrod, rail onto the base
steps_authored.text: With the sun and swing arm already on the sleeve (the lug is on the rail since Launcher 2b), slide the rail assembly's sleeve along the main axis onto the drum's d12 spigot from the outboard side (the LAUNCH dog ring is already bolted to its flange, Launcher 4) until the ring's dogs sit by the drum collar. Hang the conrod's upper eye on the lug pin and snap a printed C clip into that groove. Then slide the aim housing on from the outboard side so the sleeve end enters its bushing and the crank pin enters the conrod's lower eye (hold the swing arm with the idler pointing down and a little to the rear, clear of the output gear, and let the arm go in between the two stop posts on the housing's inner face as they come up to it); snap a printed C clip onto the crank pin and screw the housing to the deck from the top: 4 x M3 x 10 through the counterbored foot flange holes into the deck inserts. Turn the sleeve backward by hand: the arm swings the idler into the output gear, comes to rest on its engaged stop post and drives the gear without binding; forward, the arm swings out onto the other post and the output gear stays still. Then turn the wiper backward slowly: the rail rises to 47 deg, then lowers to 6 deg.

steps_authored.title: Launcher 10: wiring (battery unplugged)
steps_authored.text: Battery unplugged. Run the SW_HOME, SW_SEATED and SW_GAP wires along the rail to the pivot and leave a 150 mm loop at the main axis before they go to the frame. No wire goes onto the carriage. Each contact: one wire to its ESP32 pin (SW_HOME 21, SW_GAP 39, SW_RAIL_LOW 40, SW_SEATED 41, as params.SWITCHES), the other to GND.

steps_authored.title: Test stage 5 only: springs (NOT during assembly)
steps_authored.text: The springs go on at test stage 5, after the big gear timing, the contacts and the aim train have been checked without them. Spring guards on first (never cock with a guard off) and never fire without the tether attached (D11). Hook the back end of each spring over the inner peg of the yoke arm. Put the front hook between post and strap, lined up with the main hole, and push the 8 mm steel rod pin down through strap, hook and post. Hole set F, 8.5 mm rearward, is the fallback if the hang test shows the spring needs less stretch. The outer holes are spare. The springs are slightly stretched and hold the carriage against the stop. A drop of glue on the pin top stops it working up.

steps_authored.title: Reel bridge on rail cheek A
steps_authored.text: Press the 8 mm c1' stub into its hole in the bridge plate. Press the CSK20PP into the sprag hub (key slot on the printed rib; seen from the outboard side the inner ring must turn freely counter-clockwise and lock clockwise) and screw the hub to the plate's outboard face with four M3 x 16. Hold the bridge inboard of the main shaft stack, below the REEL gear, and bolt its box arm to the inner face of rail cheek A with two M3 x 16 (heads reached through the two holes in the arm).

steps_authored.title: Countershaft C, C1 and bevel B1
steps_authored.text: Slide countershaft C into the sprag from the outboard side, key rib in the keyway, until its collar meets the plate. Slide C1 (49 teeth) onto the D-flat so it meshes the REEL gear, then the 24-tooth bevel, teeth outboard. Turn the REEL gear by hand: C1 turns one way only (the sprag holds the other).

steps_authored.title: Take-up gears on the bridge
steps_authored.text: Slide c1' (46 teeth) onto the stub, hub outboard, meshing the bus gear. Clip the swing arm's split ring over c1's hub and put the 30-tooth swing idler on the arm pin. Push countershaft T into its bushing and slide T1 (20 teeth) and the B2 bevel onto its flat. Turn the wiper forward by hand: the idler swings into T1; backward it swings out.

steps_authored.title: Shafts along the rail
steps_authored.text: Slide the 12-tooth B1 pinion onto the front flat of u-shaft C and feed the shaft rearward through the bridge block until the pinion meshes the B1 bevel. Slide the B2 pinion onto the front flat of u-shaft T and feed it rearward through the bridge pillar until the pinion meshes B2. Both shafts reach back to the reel head.

steps_authored.title: Head frame on the rail
steps_authored.text: Screw the front plate to the spine (three M3 x 12 through the spine into the plate). Slide the front plate's bushing over the rear end of u-shaft T and bolt the plate to the rail's rear flange with four M3 x 16 into the flange inserts. Screw the mid plate to the front plate (M3 x 12).

steps_authored.title: Spool, shaft and clutch
steps_authored.text: Press a 608 into each end of the spool. Push the line end through the small hole near the inboard flange, knot it inside (figure eight) and wind 20 m on (line over the top, leaving toward the rail). Slide the clutch disk onto the outboard flat of the spool shaft (friction ring inboard), then from the other end the spool until its outboard face meets the disk, then the thrust ring, boss toward the spool. Feed the inboard end through the mid plate bushing and slide the B3 bevel onto its flat. Slide the B3 bevel for u-shaft T onto the shaft's rear flat; the two bevels mesh.

steps_authored.title: Capstan tube, drum, cup shaft and cup
steps_authored.text: Slide the capstan drum onto the front end of the capstan tube, key slot on the rib. Push the cup shaft through the tube from the front (neck end in front), slide the cup onto it (flat in the bore onto the flat, eyelet lug at the bottom, in line with the spool) and push Harry's small C-clip onto the neck.

steps_authored.title: P1, the capstan gears and the clutch lever
steps_authored.text: Press the G_b axle (8 mm rod, 26 long) into P1. Slide P1 over the capstan tube, the rear end of u-shaft C and the spool shaft end (its leg), and screw it to the spine (two M3 x 12) and to the mid plate. Put G_c (23 teeth) on the tube flat, G_a (26) on u-shaft C's flat and G_b (32) on its axle. Hang the clutch lever on the P1 post with the M3 x 16 pivot screw (it must swing), its upper arm under the drum's brake cam, the FIRM screw toward the thrust ring. Screw the LIGHT stop screw into P1 under the upper arm.

steps_authored.title: P1b, cup gear and P2
steps_authored.text: Fit P1b over the rear end of the capstan tube and screw it to the two P1 posts (M3 x 12). Slide the cup gear G_k (28 teeth, raised track forward) onto the cup shaft flat so it meshes the drum's wrap idler output with the cup at home (eyelet at the bottom). Screw P2 to the spine over the cup shaft and wrap idler ends (two M3 x 12). The cup must turn freely both ways.

steps_authored.title: SW_ARM contact
steps_authored.text: Battery unplugged. Build the printed contact (see the contact switch page): nut pressed in the base trap, lever screwed onto the pad with 2 x M3 x 10 self tapping screws, M3 x 10 contact screw with its jam nut in the lever. Screw the base to P1b's rear face with four M3 x 10. SW_ARM is closed while the cup is away from home and opens at home: the lever rides the raised track on the front of the cup gear and drops into its notch at home. Cup at home: turn the contact screw until its head just touches the nut, back it off 1.9 turns (gap about 0.9 mm) and lock the jam nut. Check with the meter: about 15 degrees of cup turn either way closes it; at home it must be open.

steps_authored.title: Shroud, line and clutch setting
steps_authored.text: Put the shroud round the spool, open side at the top toward the rail, and screw its tab to the P1 leg (M3 x 8). Lead the line from the top of the spool straight forward under the capstan drum and through the cup eyelet from behind, then forward through the pusher hole to the dart's tail cap. Wind 20 m through the eyelet once on the bench before the first shot (D49: the pack mounds in the middle). Set LIGHT with the drum at LAUNCH: turn the LIGHT stop screw until a 25 g weight hung on the line end just pulls line off slowly (0.25 N). Set FIRM with the drum at NEUTRAL: turn the FIRM screw until the line slips at 5.0 N on the luggage scale, then lock its nut.

steps_authored.title: Sensors 1: build the two contact switches (SW_RAIL_LOW, SW_GAP)
steps_authored.text: For each switch: press an M3 nut into the hex trap on the base pillar (a drop of glue), solder a wire to the nut through the side slot and lay it in the groove. Screw the lever onto the pad with 2 x M3x10 self tapping screws. Screw an M3x10 through the lever boss from the top, head down, with a ring lug and the second wire under a jam nut on top. Turn the screw until the head touches the nut, then back it off 1.9 turns (gap about 0.9 mm, 0.5 mm per turn) and lock the jam nut.

steps_authored.title: Sensors 2: SW_RAIL_LOW on the aim housing
steps_authored.text: Screw the switch base to its bracket (4 x M3x8 self tapping), lever pointing to the crank. Set the bracket foot on the housing foot extension in front of the crank. Screw it down with an M3x10 in the hole nearest the crank (self taps into the housing) and an M3x16 in the counterbored hole at the front end of the foot: down through the foot and the foot extension into the deck insert under it (the bracket's own deck screw). Turn the crank by hand (wiper backwards) to the lowest rail position: the cam lobe presses the lever tip and the meter shows the switch closed. Turn the crank about 20 deg either side: the switch must open.

steps_authored.title: Sensors 3: SW_GAP on the right rail cheek
steps_authored.text: Build SW_GAP as in Sensors 1 (its base has its own arm). Hold the arm tab on the outer face of the right rail cheek, below the big gear, and screw it on with 2 x M3x12 (heads in the counterbores). With the big gear at rest (toothless gap at the rack) the cam bump presses the lever: switch closed. Turn the gear 20 deg either way: switch open.

steps_authored.title: Sensors 4: AS5600 board
steps_authored.text: Do this after the magnet cap is on the main shaft end (drum steps): the board sits 2 mm in front of it. Battery unplugged. Plug the STEMMA QT cable into the board's connector on the +x end (the end away from the housing spine). Push the board onto the 4 pegs of the carrier, chip facing out. Drop an M3 nut into each hex pocket in the carrier back, lay the strips over the board edges (pegs through their holes) and screw each from the strip front with an M3x12 into its nut. Screw the carrier column to the aim housing spine with 2 x M3x16. Check by eye: the chip sits on the shaft axis, about 2.0 mm from the magnet face, and the cap turns free.
